## Verdict: no agent-facing context surface exists

`crimes_00016` — **Missing Agent Context** (medium, confidence 0.90, agent_risk 0.42, `pack: universal`):

```
no AGENTS.md found at repo root
no CLAUDE.md found at repo root
no .claude/skills/*/SKILL.md present
no .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md present
package.json declares bin(s): tsup, tsup-node — agents have no way to discover commands
```

It's the only `missing_agent_context` finding in the report, and it's repo-scoped — the `file: assets/cjs_shims.js` anchor is just where the detector pinned it, not the actual subject.

One thing to flag before the fix: the scan root is `evals/fixtures/04-monorepo`, but every path in the report is a single `src/` + `test/` tree (52 files, one `package.json` with `bin: tsup, tsup-node`). So there is one root to place the file at. If there really are sibling packages outside this scan root, you'd want a root AGENTS.md plus per-package ones, and you should re-scan from the true workspace root to confirm.

## Why this bites you specifically

The rest of the report explains the consequence better than the finding does. This repo is *exactly* the shape where an agent with no context makes confident-but-wrong edits:

- **Load-bearing files carry no warning.** `src/utils.ts` has fan-in 18, `src/plugin.ts` 10, `src/log.ts` 9 (`crime_00044`, `_00013`, `_00031`). `src/utils.ts` is also a 425-line God File. An agent asked to "clean up utils" will restructure a module 18 files depend on, having read none of them.
- **The tests won't catch the mistake.** 22 `weak_test_signal` findings — 12 tests with *zero* `expect`/`assert` calls (`test/example.test.ts`, `test/graphql.test.ts`, `test/shims.test.ts`, `test/tsconfig.test.ts`, `test/experimental-dts.test.ts`). Green CI here is not evidence the change is safe, and an agent has no way to know that.
- **The entry points are huge and undocumented.** `build` in `src/index.ts` is 293 lines, `runEsbuild` 237, `main` in `src/cli-main.ts` 153. `build` and `getRollupConfig` are also `name_behavior_mismatch` — read-sounding names that call `removeFiles` (`crime_00032`, `_00014`). An agent that assumes `build()` is pure will happily call it to "check something" and delete output directories.
- **Commands are undiscoverable.** Two bins, a dual esbuild + rollup pipeline, and a dts path — none of which an agent can infer from the filesystem.

Consequence in one line: the repo's dangerous parts are legible only to someone who's already worked in it, and nothing in the repo transfers that to a new agent session.

## Minimal AGENTS.md that clears the finding

Drop this at the repo root. The detector only needs the file to exist, but a stub that says nothing just converts a real gap into a silent one — this is the smallest version that's actually load-bearing.

```markdown
# AGENTS.md

Build tool: bundles TS/JS via esbuild, emits `.d.ts` via rollup/api-extractor.
Ships two bins: `tsup` and `tsup-node`.

## Commands

<!-- VERIFY these against package.json "scripts" before trusting them -->
- Install: `pnpm install`
- Build:   `pnpm build`
- Test:    `pnpm test`         # integration-heavy; each test shells out a real build
- Single:  `pnpm test <file>`

Tests are slow because they run real builds into temp dirs. Run the
narrowest file you can.

## Layout

- `src/index.ts`        — `build()` / `buildAll()` orchestration, options normalization
- `src/cli-main.ts`     — CLI arg parsing, calls into `build()`
- `src/esbuild/`        — esbuild pipeline + plugins (postcss, svelte, swc)
- `src/rollup.ts`, `src/api-extractor.ts`, `src/tsc.ts` — the `.d.ts` paths
- `src/plugin.ts`       — plugin container, shared by every pipeline
- `src/utils.ts`, `src/log.ts` — shared helpers
- `test/utils.ts`       — test harness used by 9 test files

## Before you edit

These files are load-bearing. Read the importers before restructuring;
prefer additive changes.

| File | Importers | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `src/utils.ts` | 18 | also 425 lines — split only with a plan |
| `src/plugin.ts` | 10 | shared plugin container |
| `src/log.ts` | 9 | logger construction |
| `test/utils.ts` | 9 | changing the harness breaks every test file |

## Gotchas

- `build()` (`src/index.ts`) and `getRollupConfig()` (`src/rollup.ts`) are
  **not** pure despite their names — both call `removeFiles()` and can
  delete output directories. Don't call them to "inspect" anything.
- Several tests contain no assertions. A green test run is weak evidence.
  If you change behaviour, add a real assertion rather than trusting the
  existing one.
- Entry points are large by design-debt, not by design: `build` (293 lines),
  `runEsbuild` (237), `main` (153). Read the whole function before editing
  any part of it.

## Conventions

- TypeScript, ESM source, dual CJS/ESM output.
- Don't add dependencies without checking they work in both output formats.
```

Fill in the `## Commands` block from the actual `package.json` scripts — that's the one section I couldn't derive from the scan, and a wrong command there is worse than no file.

Re-run `crimes scan --format json` after adding it; `crime_00016` should drop out and the medium count should go 38 → 37.
